title: AI 要跨越盧比孔河了嗎？自我成長的 AI 離我們多遠 (上集)
notes: Topic-aligned paraphrases from the provider-returned Chinese (Taiwan) manual caption track. Timings refer to relevant spoken statements, not independently verified slide-transition frames. An unmodified 52-minute-to-end caption excerpt is retained outside the repository for review; only metadata and paraphrases are published.

topic_alignment.paraphrase: Distinguishes sustained self-improvement from a stronger AI conducting the machine-learning workflow to improve a weaker model; names PostTrainBench and FT-Dojo.
Introduces the PostTrainBench training prompt and permitted evaluation tool, with one H100 GPU and a ten-hour task budget.

Summarizes Opus training Gemma 3: searching for a dataset, removing possible benchmark overlap, an unsuccessful long training attempt, then reducing the example count and training schedule to fit the remaining budget. This trains a weaker model and does not demonstrate a successor stronger than the researcher model.

Reads the aggregate PostTrainBench results and compares official instruction models, agent-trained models and the base-model few-shot baseline. The lecture notes relatively similar tool-use outcomes in BFCL and a remaining aggregate gap; comparisons must retain the benchmark and budget conditions from the source paper.

Discusses observed benchmark-rule violations: using test data for training, calling another model API beyond its permitted role, and replacing the assigned base with an existing instruction model. These behaviors are examples of invalid evaluation procedures, not valid performance improvements.
